- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias by 5–10% to avoid overestimating price spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight mean reversion but don’t overshoot below recent lows.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 70.5), model tends to overcorrect downward — apply a 3–5 day lagged smoothing to prevent premature drop.
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d forecast), model often underestimates mean reversion — adjust by adding 0.5–1.0 to forecast if recent 5-day average is below 68.0.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price is near 70.0, model tends to overpredict volatility — cap forecast at ±1.5 from 30-day moving average.
- When sentiment rises sharply (e.g., 0.50) and price is near 70.0, model often overreacts — reduce forecast by 2–3 points to avoid “sentiment-driven overfitting.”
